title: Labels at a Glance
transcript: We began our museum label study with a simple task. We asked visitors to find out what an unfamiliar object had been used for. In the first version of the label, a bold heading named the object. A line drawing underneath showed how a person would hold it. Before each trial, we moved a bench to a marked spot so that seated participants started at the same distance. We then compared labels that gave the object's purpose in the opening sentence with labels that placed the same information at the end. Visitors located the purpose more quickly when it came first, though the two groups remembered roughly the same amount afterwards. Our test took place in a quiet gallery, so the timing result still needs checking on busy days when other visitors may interrupt someone's view.

questions.prompt: The object's name appeared in a bold ____.
questions.explanation: 第一版标签用粗体标题标出物件名称。

questions.prompt: A line ____ showed how to hold the object.
questions.explanation: 标题下方的线描图展示了握持物件的方式。

questions.prompt: Item repositioned to standardise where seated visitors began: ____
questions.explanation: 研究人员把长凳移到标记处，使坐着的参与者从相同距离开始。

questions.prompt: What happened when the label opened with the object's purpose?
options: Visitors found the purpose faster and remembered much more.
Visitors took about the same time to find it and remembered less.
Visitors found the purpose faster and remembered about as much.
questions.answer: Visitors found the purpose faster and remembered about as much.
questions.explanation: 把用途放在开头能缩短查找时间，但两组事后记住的内容量相近。

questions.prompt: Under which conditions does the timing result still need to be checked?
options: During crowded periods when sightlines may be interrupted
During quiet periods when visitors have more time to read
During guided tours when staff explain the object aloud
questions.answer: During crowded periods when sightlines may be interrupted
questions.explanation: 试验在安静的展厅进行，讲者建议在其他参观者可能挡住视线的繁忙时段复测。
